\subsection*{Poly Hierarchy --- Collapse: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of adjacent quantifier classes]
\lean{Complexity.SigmaP_eq_PiP_of_PiP_subset_SigmaP}
\label{Complexity.SigmaP_eq_PiP_of_PiP_subset_SigmaP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PiP, Complexity.SigmaP, Complexity.compl_mem_PiP_iff}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $i$, if the class $\Pi_i^P$ is contained in $\Sigma_i^P$, then
$\Sigma_i^P=\Pi_i^P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of adjacent quantifier classes]
\lean{Complexity.SigmaP_eq_PiP_of_SigmaP_subset_PiP}
\label{Complexity.SigmaP_eq_PiP_of_SigmaP_subset_PiP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PiP, Complexity.SigmaP, Complexity.compl_mem_PiP_iff}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $i$, if the class $\Sigma_i^P$ is contained in $\Pi_i^P$, then
$\Sigma_i^P=\Pi_i^P$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{Complexity.PH, Complexity.PiP, Complexity.SigmaP, Complexity.SigmaP_mono, Complexity.SigmaP_subset_PH, Complexity.mem_PH_iff, Complexity.mem_SigmaP_of_exists, Complexity.mem_SigmaP_succ_iff}
\difficulty{6}
Let $i$ be an integer with $1 \le i$, and suppose that the class $\Sigma_i^P$ equals
$\Pi_i^P$. Then the polynomial hierarchy $\mathrm{PH}$ equals $\Sigma_i^P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Collapse of the Polynomial Hierarchy to a Level]

\proofstep
  {Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_of_SigmaP_eq_PiP}
  {context}
  {Yap83}
  {pdf-1a201b302069-p003-b003}
\uses{Complexity.PH, Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_of_SigmaP_eq_PiP, Complexity.PiP, Complexity.SigmaP, Complexity.SigmaP_eq_PiP_of_PiP_subset_SigmaP}
\difficulty{1}
Let $i\in\mathbb{N}$ with $1\le i$. If every language in $\Pi_i^\mathsf{P}$ belongs to
$\Sigma_i^\mathsf{P}$, then $\mathsf{PH}=\Sigma_i^\mathsf{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Collapse of the Polynomial Hierarchy]
\lean{Complexity.PH_eq_P_of_P_eq_NP}
\label{Complexity.PH_eq_P_of_P_eq_NP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.NP_eq_coNP_of_P_eq_NP, Complexity.P, Complexity.PH, Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_of_SigmaP_eq_PiP, Complexity.PiP, Complexity.PiP_one, Complexity.SigmaP, Complexity.SigmaP_one}
\difficulty{3}
If $\mathsf{P}=\mathsf{NP}$, then the polynomial hierarchy equals $\mathsf{P}$; that is,
$\mathsf{PH}=\mathsf{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second-level existential characterization]
\lean{Complexity.mem_SigmaP_two_iff}
\label{Complexity.mem_SigmaP_two_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PiP_one, Complexity.SigmaP, Complexity.coNP, Complexity.mem_SigmaP_succ_iff, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
For every language $L$ of binary strings, $L$ belongs to the second existential level of
the polynomial hierarchy if and only if there are natural numbers $C,c$ and a language
$L'$ in coNP such that, for every binary string $x$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent
to the existence of a binary string $u$ of length exactly $C(|x|+1)^c$ for which
$\langle x,u\rangle\in L'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Universal characterization of the second hierarchy class]
\lean{Complexity.mem_PiP_two_iff}
\label{Complexity.mem_PiP_two_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.PiP, Complexity.SigmaP_one, Complexity.mem_PiP_succ_iff, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
For every language $L$ of finite binary strings, $L\in\Pi_2^P$ if and only if there are
natural numbers $C,c$ and a language $L'\in\mathsf{NP}$ such that, for every binary
string $x$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the condition that every binary string
$u$ of length $C(|x|+1)^c$ satisfies $\langle x,u\rangle\in L'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Existential-universal characterization of the second level]
\lean{Complexity.mem_SigmaP_two_iff_exists_forall}
\statementsource{Yap83}{pdf-1a201b302069-p007-b004}
\label{Complexity.mem_SigmaP_two_iff_exists_forall}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.SigmaP, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
For every language $L$ of binary strings, $L$ belongs to the second existential level of
the polynomial hierarchy if and only if there are natural numbers $C,c$ and a language
$V$ in polynomial time such that, for every binary string $x$, membership $x\in L$ is
equivalent to the existence of a binary string $u$ of length exactly $C(|x|+1)^c$ for
which every binary string $v$ of that same length satisfies $\langle\langle
x,u\rangle,v\rangle\in V$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Universal-existential characterization of the second hierarchy class]
\lean{Complexity.mem_PiP_two_iff_forall_exists}
\label{Complexity.mem_PiP_two_iff_forall_exists}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.P, Complexity.PiP, Complexity.mem_PiP_iff, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
For every language $L$ of finite binary strings, $L\in\Pi_2^P$ if and only if there are
natural numbers $C,c$ and a language $V\in\mathsf{P}$ such that, for every binary string
$x$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the following condition: for every binary
string $u$ of length $C(|x|+1)^c$, there is a binary string $v$ of that same length for
which $\langle\langle x,u\rangle,v\rangle\in V$.
\end{theorem}
